sections.description: Introduction framing: strong decisions can fail when passed through silos, leading to a watered-down customer experience. The section sets up the core goal of uniting actions and goals to create a truly customer-centered organization.
sections.title: Silos vs. the Beloved Company

sections.description: Bliss argues for giving up siloed ownership in favor of a collective approach to delivering the customer experience. The billing experience is used as an example to show how marketing, sales, operations, customer service, and billing must all influence and be accountable for the outcome.
sections.title: Shared Ownership and Cross-Functional Metrics

sections.description: The talk emphasizes adopting a rigorous, collaborative framework for identifying and improving customer touchpoints. It references Bliss's Chief Customer Officer tools and advocates breaking the journey into manageable steps to sustain transformation and customer focus.
sections.title: Rigorous Processes and Bite-Sized Change

summary: Jeanne Bliss describes how a company becomes 'beloved' by uniting actions and goals across organizational silos to improve the customer experience. The talk emphasizes that customer impact is enhanced when cross-functional teams share ownership of the customer experience, adopt common and sometimes uncomfortable metrics, and replace siloed ownership with collaborative, process-driven rigor. A billing example illustrates how multiple departments influence a single touchpoint, while Bliss ties the approach to her Chief Customer Officer framework and advocates breaking change into bite-sized steps to make durable progress.
title: Beloved Companies: Uniting Actions & Goals Across Silos to Improve Customer Experience
topics: Billing experience as a cross-functional touchpoint
Rigorous process design for customer experience
Tools from the Chief Customer Officer framework
Avoiding wasted Energy and mediocre customer experience
Integration of marketing, sales, operations, and customer service
